how_to: The sights Journey Partner shows, picked by hand from candidates.json: only what can really be seen from a train window. Each pick names one candidate by its osm or wikidata id (tunnels and bridges by kind and km). title and note are what travellers read. season: all year, or the months it is worth looking (waterfalls flow June to September). checked: map until someone confirms it from a train. Run python3 scraper/journey_build.py to place them.

picks.title: Khada Parsi
picks.note: A Parsi gentleman on a tall cast-iron pillar, standing in the road junction since the 1860s.

picks.title: Sion Fort
picks.note: A small 17th-century British watchtower fort on the hillock just after Sion station.

picks.title: Thane Creek
picks.note: The train crosses the creek on leaving Thane, with mangroves along both banks.

picks.title: Parsik Tunnel
picks.note: 1.3 km under Parsik hill, one of the oldest railway tunnels in India still in use (1916).

picks.title: Mumbra Devi Temple
picks.note: The white temple high on the hill above Mumbra, reached by a long flight of steps.

picks.title: Matheran hills and Peb Fort
picks.note: The flat-topped Matheran range rises on the right from Badlapur to Neral. Peb Fort sits on its northern tip.

picks.title: Palasdari Dam
picks.note: The lake close to the line just after Karjat, the last flat stretch before the climb.

picks.title: Bhor Ghat begins
picks.note: The climb of about 550 m up the Sahyadri starts here, through more than 20 tunnels. Have the camera ready from now to Khandala.

picks.title: Waterfall
picks.note: One of many falls on the ghat walls in the monsoon.

picks.title: Songiri Fort
picks.note: A small hill fort guarding the old route up the ghat.

picks.title: Waterfall
picks.note: Monsoon falls across the valley.

picks.title: Rajmachi forts
picks.note: Twin forts Shrivardhan and Manaranjan on the ridge across the valley, built to watch over the Bor pass.

picks.title: Waterfall
picks.note: Monsoon falls on the far side of the valley.

picks.title: Duke's Nose
picks.note: The pointed cliff said to look like the Duke of Wellington's nose. A favourite of rock climbers.

picks.title: Waterfall
picks.note: Falls just before Khandala in the monsoon.

picks.title: Kune Falls
picks.note: A three-step waterfall of about 200 m, among the highest in India, between Khandala and Lonavala.

picks.title: Visapur Fort
picks.note: The long flat-topped fort on the right after Malavli, built by the Peshwas in the early 1700s.

picks.title: Lohagad
picks.note: The 'iron fort' with its scorpion-tail ridge, just behind Visapur.

picks.title: Bhaja Caves
picks.note: 22 Buddhist rock-cut caves from the 2nd century BC, as small dark openings in the hillside above Bhaja village.

picks.title: Ghorawadi hill and caves
picks.note: A rocky hill with a Shiva temple and Buddhist caves near the top.

picks.title: Mula River at Dapodi
picks.note: The train crosses the Mula beside the old stone Harris Bridge.

picks.title: Mula–Mutha river
picks.note: The last river crossing, just before Pune Junction.
